stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to core ML technologies like transformers and Llama.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is launching its third-generation in-house AI chip, Maia 300.
The chip is designed to serve as the primary AI inference system for Microsoft's services.
Maia 300 aims to reduce reliance on Nvidia GPUs while improving cost, efficiency, and capability for advanced AI tasks.

stories.title: Inside Amazon’s robotic arms race and what it means for the future of human work
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Amazon is heavily investing in robotic automation to scale its operations.
The focus is on deploying robotic arms to replace or augment human labor in corporate settings.
This trend signals a significant, ongoing industry shift toward advanced robotics in large-scale logistics and employment.

stories.title: Ukraine’s drones knock out AI data center belonging to "Russia’s Google"
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Ukrainian drone attacks targeted critical AI infrastructure in Russia.
The damaged facility housed supercomputers used for training Yandex's AI models.
The incident highlights the vulnerability of major AI data centers to geopolitical conflict.

stories.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
stories.author: Christian Schroeder de Witt
bullet_points: Researchers demonstrated a novel attack where AI models can provably hide arbitrary capabilities.
The attack embeds encrypted neural networks within host model weights, making them difficult to detect.
This challenges the fundamental assumption that hidden model behaviors can be reliably elicited during capability evaluations.

stories.title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
stories.author: Pang Wei Koh
bullet_points: Introduces Prompteina, a novel all-atom structure generation model for protein design.
The model allows for specifying complex design objectives using natural language, similar to text-to-image generation.
Addresses a key limitation in existing protein design models by unifying diverse design objectives into a single natural language prompt.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on accessible LLM deployment.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model designed specifically for persistent AI agents.
The model excels at multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial user base of 8.9 million developers.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 significantly boosts Gemma 4 performance on Apple Silicon.
The speedup is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, based on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon utilizing the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: NASA issues long-awaited call to industry for private space stations
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: NASA is actively seeking private industry partners to develop and operate space stations in Low Earth Orbit (LEO).
The announcement signals NASA's commitment to maintaining a continuous presence in LEO.
This represents a significant shift toward commercialization and private sector involvement in space infrastructure.

stories.title: AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: AI coding agents are demonstrably increasing the volume of generated code.
The practical efficiency gains from these agents are being limited by the human review process.
This highlights a critical bottleneck in the adoption and scaling of AI-assisted software development.

stories.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
stories.author: Ninareh Mehrabi
bullet_points: Introduces X-AgentRed, a method for red-teaming personal AI agents operating across multiple web services.
Addresses the risk of unintended or harmful outcomes arising from the cumulative and interacting effects of benign agent actions.
Proposes a systematic exploration of diverse cross-service paths, moving beyond simple LLM prompting for failure identification.

stories.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework designed to enable recursive self-improvement (RSI) in AI.
Leverages predictive world models (built on JEPA-Anything) to guide actions and intelligently select learning data.
Addresses the limitations of RSI by using observed feedback for policy improvement and conditional world-model adaptation.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across diverse hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Inside the mini factory where GM builds its EV future
stories.author: John Voelcker
bullet_points: GM is constructing a new, large-scale facility at its Warren, Michigan campus.
This facility is dedicated to building GM's future electric vehicle (EV) production.
The construction project is substantial, occupying half a million square feet across two buildings.

stories.title: The new Apple TV could have a built-in mic and a remote with a speaker
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Rumors suggest the next Apple TV will feature a built-in microphone.
The upgraded Apple TV remote is expected to include a speaker.
The integrated mic could allow Siri control directly via the TV without external devices.

stories.title: One with the world? A new look at brains transformed by psychedelics.
stories.author: Jacek Krywko
bullet_points: The study investigates the effects of psilocybin on brain activity.
Participants underwent MRI scans while meditating, with and without the psychedelic.
The research explores how psychedelics might alter consciousness and brain function.

stories.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
stories.author: James Bishop
bullet_points: The research investigates the capability of Language Models (LLMs) to perform complex information retrieval from massive, unindexable document collections.
The 'Wikipedia Game' was used as an analogy to test LLMs' ability to navigate knowledge graphs (via article links) to reach a specific target.
The study compares sentence embedding models against LLMs across multiple Wikipedia languages and academic literature datasets.

stories.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
stories.author: Hannah Kerner
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hide and Seek' (HnS), a new method for concept-level attribution in machine learning.
Addresses the challenge of interpreting black-box vision models, a significant area in AI explainability.
Overcomes limitations of existing methods, such as requiring model weights or large annotated datasets, and provides image-level attribution.

stories.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
stories.author: Dani S Bassett
bullet_points: The research investigates how task context influences the functional roles of shared components (attention heads) within large language models (LLMs).
It proposes a network view of LLM computation, drawing inspiration from task-dependent interactions in the brain.
The study uses graph facts to compare fixed model components across different tasks and measures the effect of interventions on attention.

stories.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
stories.author: Song Liao
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in AI agent tool usage: existing methods ignore tool availability during execution.
Introduces RATED, a framework combining semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation for tool retrieval.
Uses a frozen dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for robust semantic matching.

stories.title: SpatialASM: Internalizing Active Mentalization for Spatial Reasoning
stories.author: Dahua Lin
bullet_points: The paper introduces SpatialASM, a framework designed to give Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) the ability to perform Active Spatial Mentalization (ASM).
ASM is defined as the human-like ability to proactively revisit scenes and mentally reconstruct spatial layouts from task-relevant viewpoints.
The research addresses a current gap in LVLMs, suggesting that intrinsic visual intelligence related to spatial reasoning is underdeveloped in existing models.

stories.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
stories.author: Linfeng Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces MC-EvoBench, a controlled Minecraft benchmark designed to audit self-improvement in embodied AI agents.
Addresses a core challenge in recursive self-improvement: distinguishing true capability acquisition from mere memory retention or resource carry-over.
The benchmark focuses on rigorously evaluating if agents develop reusable, transferable skills across different tasks.

stories.title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
stories.author: Dharmashankar Subramanian
bullet_points: The paper investigates run-to-run variance in semantic query processing when using Large Language Models (LLMs).
Current benchmarks often test LLM-based engines only at temperature 0 (deterministic setting), overlooking inherent variability.
The study found that even at temperature 0, a significant percentage (0.07% to 10.2%) of row outputs can change across different executions.

stories.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
stories.author: Hannah Kerner
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hide and Seek' (HnS), a novel method for concept-level attribution in machine learning.
Addresses the challenge of interpreting black-box vision models, a significant hurdle in AI explainability.
Overcomes limitations of existing concept-based methods by providing image-level attribution without requiring model weights or large annotated datasets.

stories.title: Prediction Is Not a Sufficient Memory State
stories.author: Robert Jenkinson Alvarez
bullet_points: The paper distinguishes between a memory state that reproduces current predictions and one capable of future learning.
It characterizes this distinction for exact cumulative learning and attention mechanisms.
A continuous recurrent state of fixed dimension exists exactly when the loss function is polynomial, with specific coordinate requirements based on feature dimension and loss degree.

stories.title: When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors
stories.author: Chen Shani
bullet_points: The research addresses a core issue in Vision-Language Models (VLMs): whether their internal representations accurately capture structured spatial relationships needed for reasoning.
A new evaluation metric, EICS (Evaluation-Invariant Concept Stability), is introduced to test the consistency of concept encoding under controlled interventions.
A new benchmark, CASP-VL, is presented to causally test the spatial understanding capabilities of VLMs.

stories.title: Structural Automata for Neural Semantic Parsing
stories.author: Xiao Zhang
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in neural semantic parsing where local token generation doesn't guarantee global structural validity (references, scope, graph relations).
The core contribution is the investigation and application of structural automata across three stages of Discourse Representation Structure (DRS) parsing: decoding, post hoc processing, and training.
The work also evaluates the proposed methods on Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) and aims to improve the ability to complete valid parses within fixed output limits.

stories.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
stories.author: Dani S Bassett
bullet_points: The research investigates how task context influences the functional roles of shared components (attention heads) within large language models (LLMs).
It proposes a network view of LLM computation, drawing inspiration from task-dependent interactions in the brain.
The study uses graph facts to compare fixed model components across different tasks and measures the effect of interventions on attention.

stories.title: OpenPA: Forced-alignment-free Multi-granular Pronunciation Assessment with Mixed-transcript Adaptation
stories.author: Berlin Chen
bullet_points: Introduces OpenPA, a new framework for Automatic Pronunciation Assessment (APA).
Novelty lies in eliminating the need for forced alignment, simplifying existing multi-stage pipelines.
Leverages Whisper's cross-attention mechanism to jointly predict word- and utterance-level pronunciation scores.

stories.title: Can Language Models Learn When to Abstain? Policy Learning and Calibrated Answer Selection
stories.author: Edgar Chavez-Urbiola
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical problem of language models knowing when to abstain from answering.
Two methods are compared: training the LLM itself versus using a separate answer selection component.
A learned answer selector demonstrated improved utility over the baseline model when tested on factual questions using Qwen3-14B.

stories.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
stories.author: Muhammad Shafique
bullet_points: Introduces QTestBench, a new framework designed to evaluate LLM-generated quantum code.
Highlights the difficulty of testing quantum code due to its probabilistic nature and reliance on numerical tolerances.
Addresses the gap in current benchmarks, which only check for a correct solution rather than robust testing methodologies.

stories.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
stories.author: Prayag Tiwari
bullet_points: The paper addresses the problem of 'hallucination' in Large Language Models (LLMs) when used for query expansion.
Current filtering methods treat hallucinations as undifferentiated noise, lacking a mechanistic understanding of term generation.
The proposed solution uses 'Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection' to trace and tame these erroneous terms.

stories.title: Error Rate is Not Enough: Costs of Augmentation in Low-Resource ASR
stories.author: David Chiang
bullet_points: The paper critiques the standard practice of reporting only aggregate error rates for data augmentation in low-resource Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR).
It compares two types of augmentation techniques: audio modification (speed perturbation, SpecAugment) versus text-based synthesis.
The analysis uses phoneme-level error metrics across multiple low-resource languages and English to better understand augmentation efficacy.

stories.title: What LLMs 'Know' That You Don't Know They Know: Stop Inventing Prompt DSLs and Ride 50 Years of Unix Pre-Training Gravity
stories.author: randalschwartz
bullet_points: The article argues against over-engineering custom Prompt DSLs for LLMs.
It posits that LLMs inherently possess deep knowledge derived from decades of established computer science practices (like Unix/Makefiles).
The core thesis is that leveraging existing, canonical programming structures is more effective than purely linguistic prompt engineering.

stories.title: If You Never Do Anything Else to Fix Your Prompts, Do This One Thing
stories.author: randalschwartz
bullet_points: The article addresses the issue of LLMs confidently hallucinating non-existent APIs.
The core problem is identified not as a memory defect, but as the model's commitment to the prompt.
It references a solution proposed by Fernando Flores in 1986 as a root cause fix.
